subject: Vocabulary
topic: Spelling Correction — Commonly Misspelt Words (W11 B1)

questions.explanation: C is correct. ACCOMMODATION (double 'c', double 'm') is the correct spelling. Memory tip: 'accommodation' can accommodate two 'c's and two 'm's. Common error: single 'c' or single 'm'. The root: ac + commodation (from Latin commodus = convenient).

B is correct. NECESSARY (one 'c', double 's'). Memory tip: It is necessary to wear one Collar and two Socks = 1C + 2S. Common error: double 'c' and single 's' (neccesary), or double 'c' and double 's' (neccessary).

D is correct. EMBARRASSMENT (double 'r', double 's'). Memory tip: she Really Blushed — double 'r' and double 's'. Common errors: single 'r' with double 's' (embarrasment), or adding a phantom 'e' before 'ment' (embarrassement). The suffix '-ment' is added directly to 'embarrass' without any vowel: embarrass + ment.

B is correct. OCCURRENCE (double 'c', double 'r', ending in '-ence'). Root: occur (double 'r' when suffix added) + rence. Rule: when a word ends in a consonant-vowel-consonant pattern and the last syllable is stressed (oc-CUR), double the final consonant before a vowel suffix: occur + rence = occurrence. Trap: -ance vs -ence: 'occurrence' ends in -ence (not -ance).

C is correct. PRIVILEGE (no 'd', middle syllable is '-vil-', not '-vel-'). From Latin privilegium = private + law. Breakdown: privi + lege. Common error: adding 'd' (privilege → privilege without d); also 'privelege' (wrong middle vowel). Memory tip: 'privi-LEGE' — you need a 'leg' to stand on to enjoy a privilege.

C is correct. RECOMMEND (one 'c', double 'm'). Breakdown: re + commend. 'Commend' has double 'm'; adding 're-' keeps one 'c'. Memory tip: re + com + mend. Common error: double 'c' (reccommend) or single 'm' (recomend). The word 'commend' itself has double 'm', and 'recommend' = re + commend.

D is correct. EXISTENCE (ending in '-ence', not '-ance'). Related words: exist → existence; resistant → resistance; persistent → persistence. Rule: '-ence' after the verb 'exist'. The '-ence/-ance' distinction is one of the most tested spelling rules in SSC CGL. Memory: EXIST + ENCE (all 'e's: exIst → existEnce). Trap: 'existance' = the most common error — wrong suffix '-ance'.

questions.stem: Choose the MISSPELT word among the options:
questions.explanation: C is correct (as the MISSPELT word). MILLENIUM is incorrect; the correct spelling is MILLENNIUM (double 'l', double 'n'). Milli (thousand) + ennium (year). From Latin: mille = thousand + annus = year. Both doubled consonants: millEnnium. Verify the others: Questionnaire ✓ (questionnaire = question + naire); Lieutenant ✓ (tricky but correct with 'lieu'); Entrepreneur ✓ (French origin).

C is correct. DEFINITELY (from 'definite' + -ly). The base word is 'DEFINITE' — note it ends in 'ite', not 'ate'. Adding '-ly': definite + ly = definitely. Memory: 'definITE + ly = definITEly'. Common error: 'definately' = people pronounce it wrong and spell it wrong; 'definitly' = drops the 'e'.

questions.stem: Choose the MISSPELT word among the options:
questions.explanation: D is correct (as the MISSPELT word). INDEPENDANT is wrong; correct spelling is INDEPENDENT (ending in '-ent', not '-ant'). Memory: in + depend + ENT. Other '-ent' words: dependent, student, president. Verify others: Conscientious ✓ (con + science + tious); Supersede ✓ (note: NOT 'supercede' — common error; only supersede); Perseverance ✓ (per + severe + ance).
